footer.blurb: A tiny, open, pocket-sized computer you write your own apps for. Hand-built limited run — not for sale.
footer.madeBy: {os} {fw} · firmware ~90% vibecoded by Claude (Opus 4.8 + Fable 5) with m4l3vich.

hero.tagline: Is it a game? A beeper? A pocket computer? All of it, actually — and more.
hero.lead: J++Device is a tiny open handheld you can write apps for. It's based on ESP32-C6 Super Mini soldered to a custom mainboard and has a keypad, small monochrome OLED, an SD card and an RTC module. It also has a custom firmware for it called {strongStart}JPPDOS{strongEnd}.
hero.scarceRest: that were handed out during J++Meetup 2026 in Moscow. You can build your own device, though.
hero.caption: 128×64 OLED · 5 buttons · 512KB SRAM

whatIsIt.title: Everything you can wish for.
whatIsIt.lead: Well, almost. You can make it do everything it's able to.

open.title: DIY and customise it.
open.body: {strongStart}All CAD files and firmware sources are out there.{strongEnd} You can make a better enclosure or print it in your favourite colour. Make an app to control your PC or a smart light or a vibe coding agent. Have at it!

game.title: Play games on it?
game.body: It ain't got no AAA games on it, but if you're bored you can {strongStart}play some Tetris or Pong.{strongEnd} If you have the mad luck to be around an another J++Device user you can {strongStart}play multiplayer Battleships!{strongEnd}

specs.title: Small, monochrome, and open on purpose.
specs.lead: The signature look is real, not styling: a see-through PETG shell over visible electronics, a 1-bit OLED, and orange keycaps as the one pop of colour.

input.detail: 5-way directional pad — up / down / left / right + center

storage.detail: 128 MB microSD card included (apps + data) · internal flash for settings

sound.detail: Passive piezo buzzer (PC speaker) — tones, tunes, selectable startup jingles

radio.detail: Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5 LE, Zigbee, Thread, plus ESP-NOW device-to-device

connection.detail: Single USB-C port — charging, flashing, and host tools

power.detail: 1000 mAh Li-Po (102050) with on-device battery percentage and a physical battery kill-switch to prevent degradation.

enclosure.detail: 3D-printed transparent PETG shell with orange PLA keycaps — internals visible.

openSource.title: One open device. One open firmware. Endless tinkering.
openSource.lead: Everything is public — firmware, docs, and the enclosure CAD. Openness is the pitch: the site points outward to GitHub, not inward to a store.
openSource.caption: Install or update it right from your browser, once the web flasher lands.

jppdos.name: JPPDOS
jppdos.body1: The operating system this whole page is about: a launcher, sandboxed apps, games, the demoscene, and the full SDK.
jppdos.body: A firmware based on ESP-IDF intended to run apps that make full use of the available hardware through App SDK. Has a few built-in apps: Games, Fable Demoscene, MeetApp.

firmware.name: JPPDOS firmware
firmware.body: Full open source for the operating system — launcher, apps, SDK, and all built-ins.

docs.name: App developer docs
docs.body: Platform overview, MicroPython and native-C guides, manifest reference, and a complete SDK reference.

cad.name: Enclosure CAD
cad.body: All 3D-printable case files (Autodesk Fusion) — print the transparent shell and orange keycaps yourself.

web_flasher.name: Web flasher
web_flasher.body: Install JPPDOS or a custom firmware from your browser over USB — no toolchain.

web_ui.name: Management Web UI
web_ui.body: A JPPD-SMP web app to manage a connected device — SD files, device info, time sync — from the browser.

apps.title: Loaded and ready on first boot.
apps.lead: Nine games, an oldskool megademo, contact exchange, a Wi-Fi file drive — all in the launcher out of the box. This hardware is meant to be seen.
apps.demosceneNote: 8 scenes · sine scrolltext · 4×4 Bayer dither · looping chiptune

games.name: Games
games.body: A hub of nine games loaded on demand — Tetris, Pong, Snake, and more. Several play two-device multiplayer over Bluetooth, and per-game high scores are saved.

demoscene.name: Demoscene
demoscene.body: An oldskool megademo made {strongStart}entirely by Claude Fable 5{strongEnd}. 8 auto-cycling scenes — 3D starfield, plasma, rotozoomer, tunnel, wireframe cube, doom-fire and raster-bar credits — plus a sine-wave scrolltext and a looping chiptune. All integer math on a 1-bit screen.

meetapp.name: MeetApp
meetapp.body: Exchange contact identities with another J++Device over Bluetooth, backed by real Ed25519 cryptographic identity.

webdav.name: WebDAV server
webdav.body: Turn the device into a Wi-Fi file drive to move files on and off the SD card straight from your computer.

settings.name: Settings
settings.body: Wi-Fi, NTP time, sleep timers, sound and startup jingle, backup/restore, factory reset, user name, and a single-app kiosk lock mode.

sdk_test.name: SDK Test apps
sdk_test.body: Two live demos — one MicroPython, one native C — that exercise every SDK call. The fastest way to see the whole API in action on real hardware.

developers.lead: Write it in MicroPython or native C, drop the folder on the SD card, and it shows up in the launcher. Here's a complete clock app — the same program, both languages.
developers.hint: manifest.json + one entry file per app · ~21 chars × 7 lines of text, plus a full pixel canvas
developers.madeBy: {os} was ~90% vibecoded by Claude (Opus 4.8 + Fable 5), together with m4l3vich — the firmware, the SDK, the built-in apps, and this demoscene. You can vibecode some stuff too!

noPermission.body: Drawing, input, buzzer, LED, the key-value store, IPC, and device status all work with nothing to declare.

prompted.body: Internet access, Bluetooth, background execution, and full-SD access ask the user the first time they are used — and can be denied without crashing the app.

getOne.title: You get it or you make it.
getOne.lead: The J++Device isn't and never will be sold.
getOne.way1Body: Print the transparent shell and orange keycaps from the published CAD, source the parts, and flash JPPDOS over USB-C. Everything you need — firmware, docs, and case files — is on GitHub.
getOne.way2Body: m4l3vich handed out 20 hand-built units in person to the J++ community and friends at {meetup} in {city}. Each unit is numbered and carries a signed, write-once identity chip.
getOne.provBody: Each handed-out unit proves it's a genuine numbered piece from an on-device verification mechanism — a signed Ed25519 identity that survives factory reset and reflashing. The identity can be verified through a serial connection or online.

manager.title: J++Device Manager
manager.lead: Flash firmware, manage the SD card, and install apps — all from your browser over Web Serial. Connect your J++Device with a USB-C cable and give consent on the device when asked.
manager.unsupported: Your browser doesn't support the Web Serial API. Please use a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Brave) to connect to your device.
manager.connectHint: Connect your J++Device over USB-C, then open a session. You'll be asked to press Allow on the device.
manager.consent: Waiting for consent on the device — press Allow…
manager.denied: Consent was denied on the device.
manager.appRunning: Close any running app on the device, then try again.

flash.title: Flash firmware
flash.body: Select a JPPDOS merged firmware image (e.g. build/merged.bin) and write it to the device. Flashing replaces the operating system — make sure you have the right image. The device will reboot and re-enumerate when done.
flash.done: Firmware flashed. The device is rebooting.
flash.writeHint: Download a JPPDOS release first — the merged 2 MB image is what you flash.
flash.noFile: Choose a firmware image to begin.

files.title: SD card
files.body: Browse, upload, and download files on the device SD card. All access goes through a JPPD-SMP session and the consent dialog.
files.downloadBad: Downloaded but CRC-32 mismatch — the file may be corrupt.

apps.title: Install an app
apps.body: Upload an app package — a folder with manifest.json and its entry binary — or a .zip archive containing one. The package is validated in the browser before anything is sent to the device.
apps.folderHint: Pick the app folder that contains manifest.json (Folder picker works in Chrome/Edge).

errors.denied: Consent was denied on the device.
errors.appRunning: An app is currently running — exit to the launcher first.

oled.ariaLabel: A 128×64 monochrome OLED running the J++Device demoscene.
